assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology, from the proglucagon-derived peptide to the incretin effect and long-acting agonists, has produced a new class of therapy for type 2 diabetes and obesity with large cardiometabolic outcome benefits. The work is original, clear and clinically transformative, which fits the prize's emphasis on benefit to humankind.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and the active GLP-1(7-36) form), Drucker (GLP-1 biology and receptor pharmacology, GLP-2) and Mojsov (peptide identification and early synthesis) are the strongest basic-science trio from the supplied credits. Knudsen's liraglutide/semaglutide work is mainly industrial drug development and is left out of this configuration. Priority claims around Mojsov, Habener and Drucker are disputed and I cannot independently verify the details.
assessment.maturity: Efficacy is confirmed by many independent large randomized trials and by real-world use, and the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Disputed priority among the early proglucagon/GLP-1 peptide discoverers; the three-person limit leaves out some contributors including Habener and Knudsen.
Long-term safety and durability of obesity treatment are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology causal, cell-type-specific control of activity with millisecond precision. It underlies mechanistic work on circuits in health and disease and has begun to reach clinical use in retinal restoration. The tool is original and widely adopted.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and its deployment in neurons as a general tool (Deisseroth, Boyden) are separate contributions. Miesenböck's earlier light-gated approach adds a further claim. Six credited names exceed the three-laureate limit, so any configuration leaves out credible contributors. I favour a mix of molecular discovery and neuronal implementation.
assessment.maturity: Methodology has been confirmed independently and extensively across labs and species for over a decade, so timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Unresolved allocation among Bamberg, Boyden, Miesenböck and the three proposed names.
Clinical translation is still early, so the case rests mainly on its role as a research tool.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells that produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies are a conceptual and clinical breakthrough in cancer immunotherapy, with several approved products. Impact is high and the principle (engineering immune cells as living drugs) is generalizable.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical CD19 CAR-T and costimulatory design in patients) and Sadelain (CAR design with CD28 costimulation, preclinical proof of concept) are central. Rosenberg contributed adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T-cell trials, but the CAR-specific claim is less direct. Earlier CAR concepts (Eshhar, Kuwana) are not in the supplied credits and I cannot weigh them here.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and independent outcome data support it. Long-term follow-up is maturing, and toxicity and solid-tumour limits remain active areas.
uncertainties: Whether Rosenberg or foundational CAR originators belong in a fair configuration.
Late toxicities, secondary malignancies and limited solid-tumour efficacy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splicing-modulating antisense therapy for spinal muscular atrophy (nusinersen) converted a lethal infant neurodegenerative disease into a treatable one, and demonstrated a rational pathway from RNA mechanism to drug. From a neurological perspective the clinical effect is striking and the concept extends to other genetic diseases.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the ISS-N1/SMN2 splicing mechanism and the ASO target with Bennett's group; Bennett led antisense chemistry and development at Ionis. The two-person configuration is clean in the supplied credits, though others (e.g. Hua, Singh) contributed.
assessment.maturity: Approval since 2016, long-term clinical follow-up and independent replication of the mechanism make it reasonably mature. The field is still young, so some may judge it a little early.
uncertainties: Contributions of other mechanism and chemistry scientists not listed here.
Long-term durability and the balance of basic versus industrial contribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: PCSK9 combined the discovery of a gain-of-function disease gene, human loss-of-function genetics showing lifelong low LDL cholesterol with protection from coronary disease, and approved inhibitors. It is an exemplary case of human genetics validating a target.
assessment.attribution: Abifadel, Boileau and colleagues first linked PCSK9 mutations to hypercholesterolemia, Seidah identified and characterized the proprotein convertase, and Hobbs and Cohen provided the loss-of-function genetics and mechanism. The five credited names cannot all be accommodated, and the allocation among them is contested. I lean to the genetic-validation and biochemical axis but acknowledge the French discovery claim.
assessment.maturity: Outcome trials of antibody inhibitors and siRNA are confirmed, and the biology is stable. Recognition is plausible now, though statins and LDL-receptor work were already honoured (1985).
uncertainties: Priority of Abifadel, Boileau and colleagues versus the Dallas group.
Incremental clinical benefit over statins and cost may temper enthusiasm.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of BCL11A as the fetal-to-adult haemoglobin switch repressor led to an approved gene-editing therapy for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassaemia. It is a clean path from human genetic variation to mechanism to cure.
assessment.attribution: Orkin and Sankaran established BCL11A's role in HbF silencing, and Bauer developed the enhancer-editing therapeutic strategy. Thein's contribution is more clinical and genetic-association oriented and is left out of this configuration. Earlier HbF genetic mapping work might also deserve credit, which the supplied credits do not show.
assessment.maturity: Approval is recent and the long-term durability and safety of edited cells are still being assessed, so recognition may be somewhat premature, though the mechanism is well confirmed.
uncertainties: Long-term safety and access of the gene-edited therapy.
Allocation between mechanism discovery and therapeutic editing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib proved that targeting a defining oncogenic kinase can produce durable responses in a cancer, and it launched the era of molecularly targeted therapy. Its clinical impact on chronic myeloid leukaemia is dramatic and enduring.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound development), Druker (clinical translation) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and further inhibitors) form a credible set. The BCR-ABL discovery (Rowley, Nowell, Hungerford, Groffen, Baltimore and others) is not in this candidate's credit, which leaves a fair-attribution gap in the origin of the target.
assessment.maturity: Long-term survival data over two decades confirm it. Timing is mature, and the Lasker Award has already recognized it. The Committee has not honoured the targeted-therapy concept, which makes it plausible.
uncertainties: Attribution gap regarding the discovery of the BCR-ABL fusion and its oncogenic role.
Possibly overshadowed by more recent therapeutic paradigms.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency deep brain stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus or thalamus is a major functional treatment for advanced Parkinson's disease and tremor, and it is now applied in other circuit disorders. Its clinical benefit is large and sustained in selected patients. I recognise my own field overlap and weigh it only on the common criteria.
assessment.attribution: Benabid introduced high-frequency stimulation clinically, but the supplied credit lists only him. The physiological and basal-ganglia model work (e.g. of DeLong and others) and the subthalamic target rationale are not credited here, so a single-laureate prize may understate shared authorship of the concept.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent clinical confirmation and randomized trials support it, so it is mature. Prior Lasker recognition indicates field acceptance.
uncertainties: Single-person attribution may not fairly capture the basal-ganglia circuit work behind the target.
Benefit is symptomatic rather than disease-modifying.
